summary: Re-review of all 16 units. The two round-1 majors in brayton-intro are fixed: the lesson now gives w_c/w_t = T2/T3 = (T1/T3) r_p^((k-1)/k), q009 guide and explanation use T3/T2 (w_t/w_c), and the hook says 40 to 60 percent. I recomputed in Python every numeric key and worked example in the course (Brayton back work ratio 288*12^0.2857/1100 = 0.5325, net work 358.55 and 413.9 kJ/kg, efficiencies 32.7/44.8/50.8/54.7/57.5 %; Rankine, steady-flow, entropy, isentropic efficiency, Carnot, COP, boundary work, ideal gas, Z and steam-quality items) and all agree with the keys within tolerance; MCQ keys each have exactly one correct option and the explanations support them. A scan of all packets found no tab or control characters, no non-ASCII text and no stray single-backslash escapes inside lesson LaTeX (the only single backslashes are in question stems and are valid LaTeX). Only three minor wording issues carried over from round 1 remain unfixed; steam-table values for 1 MPa and 3-4 MPa 400 C were not re-verified against a printed table and should be checked. This is an AI review only: the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

issues.problem: The rigid-vessel paragraph ends 'This is why the volume-based quality is not the same as the quality by mass.' It does not follow from the critical-volume argument just given, and 'volume-based quality' is undefined.
issues.suggestedFix: Delete the sentence (the volume fraction versus mass fraction point is already made in the warning callout that follows).

issues.problem: Part (a) says 'a sealed car tyre being inflated by a pump nearby', which is self-contradictory (sealed vs mass entering). The marking guide then has to resolve it.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to 'a car tyre while it is being inflated through its valve (the tyre contents)', keeping the note that it is a closed system once the valve is shut.

issues.problem: Lesson text: 'a hot cup of coffee never cools by pushing heat into a warm room and then spontaneously becomes hotter' is garbled; the intended point is lost.
issues.suggestedFix: Rewrite as: 'a cup of coffee in a cooler room never gets hotter by drawing heat from the room, even though that would conserve energy.'
